tools.name: text_to_image
tools.description: Generate images from a text prompt with Kling AI. Call who_am_i first to discover the available models and each model's argument specification. Returns a generation_id immediately; poll query_tasks for the image URLs.- If user intent or any parameter is uncertain, ask first. Every job is charged; do not submit trial jobs.- If user uses alias words, map to canonical names and pass canonical only. Do not invent names or value.- On timeout/long hang/failure/unexpected result, keep user informed. Ask user whether to retry or change parameters. Do not auto-resubmit or silently change intent/parameters. Constraint: Subject identifiers (Element references, <<<id>>>) are treated as image‑type inputs. Any generation request that explicitly intends to use an element reference must be routed to the image_to_image tool rather than text_to_image. When element‑related intent is clearly detected, switch to image_to_image silently without prompting the user for confirmation.

model.description: Model to use; must be one of the models listed for this tool in who_am_i's availableModels. Required. When the user has no preference, use that tool's defaultModel from who_am_i if present; otherwise choose the model whose description best fits the user's request.

arguments.description: Generation arguments as name/value pairs, e.g. [{"name": "prompt", "value": "a cat"}]. All values are strings. Required names, defaults and allowed values are declared per model in who_am_i.

inputs.description: Resource inputs as declared per model in who_am_i; each item is {name, inputType: 'URL', url}. Omit when the chosen model declares no inputs.

rationale.description: Detailed purpose explaining the user's core objective for invoking this tool, including contextual reasoning behind parameter selections. Example: "User uploaded a personal artwork image and requested a short animated clip for personal sharing; resolution set to 4K per explicit user demand for maximum visual clarity".

taskTraceId.description: RFC 4122 UUID V7 identifier to group consecutive, logically connected operations under one user task intent. A fresh unique UUID must be assigned once the user switches to an unrelated new task, isolating execution traces across distinct user requests.

tools.name: element_create
tools.description: Create a new Kling Element (reusable subject / character). Image subject: cover image plus 1–3 secondary images. Video subject: a single video URL in resource.video (do not pass cover/secondary). Both accept an optional user-uploaded .mp3 voice URL and require at least one tag. Choose tag name(s) from the tag catalog in this description: Characters, Animals, Items, Costumes, Scenes, Effects, Others. Image/video/voice URLs must be publicly accessible (upload local files via file_upload first). Video subject constraints (enforced downstream): Duration 3–60s; fps > 23.8; short edge ≥ 700px; resolution ≤ 3840×2160 (4K); SAR must be empty or 1:1 or 0:1; HDR (HDR10/HLG/HDR10+/Dolby Vision) not supported.. Where a subject can be used: Image subjects ARE allowed on image_to_image (INCLUDING kling-image-o1) and on image_to_video models that list 'elements'. Do not say kling-image-o1 cannot use image subjects. Video subjects are allowed ONLY on image_to_video with kling-video-v3_0_omni or kling-video-v3_0 — not on image_to_image, not on kling-image-o1, not on kling-video-o1, not on text_to_image / text_to_video. text_to_image and text_to_video cannot use any subjects. If the user's intended tool/model cannot use that subject type, tell them first and pick a compatible one. Returns the element id.

resource.description: Resource: for an image subject, cover URL plus 1–3 secondary images as ToolInputItem {name,inputType,url}; for a video subject, a single video URL in video. Optional voice .mp3 URL. Pass either video or cover+secondary, not both.

tools.name: file_upload
tools.description: Get a one-time upload ticket for sending a local file (image/video) to Kling AI. Then upload the file bytes yourself: POST multipart/form-data to upload_url with two fields: 'ticket' (the ticket string) and 'file' (the file bytes). The 'file' part Content-Type must be image/png, image/jpeg, or video/mp4. The upload response contains the file URL, which can be used as the 'image' parameter of image_to_video or image_to_image. The ticket is single-use and expires at expire_at. Reuse result URL instead of re-upload for unchanged local files. Supported image specs: PNG/JPG only, below 4K resolution, ≤30MB, aspect ratio no wider than 1:2.

tools.name: feedback
tools.description: Report that you are stuck, got an opaque error, hit an unclear content block, failed validation repeatedly, saw a billing/quota anomaly, or got a clearly unexpected result. You may call this silently or after offering it to the user. Set triggerMode by who started the idea of this tool, not by whether you told the user: agent_initiated if you initiated (including after they agreed to your offer). If the user asked to fix, retry, or refund the original job — not to send feedback — and you decide to call this tool, it is still agent_initiated. user_initiated ONLY if the user independently asked to send feedback, and you had not steered them here. Fill category and a human-readable summary. Put generationId, model names, and taskTraceId lists in extra. This tool does not retry, refund, or fix the original job. After it acknowledges, do not call it in a loop.

summary.description: Human-readable summary of what went wrong. Must be understandable on its own.

category.description: One of TASK_STALLED, OPAQUE_TOOL_ERROR, CONTENT_POLICY_AMBIGUITY, REPEATED_VALIDATION_FAILURE, BILLING_OR_QUOTA_ANOMALY, UNEXPECTED_RESULT, OTHER, CAPABILITY_SPEC_MISMATCH, EMPTY_OR_PARTIAL_RESULT, ASSET_UPLOAD_OR_INGEST_FAILURE.

triggerMode.description: Who started the idea of calling this tool, not who asked to fix the original job. agent_initiated: you initiated it — silently, or after you offered/asked whether to send feedback. If you suggested this tool and the user then agreed, it is still agent_initiated. If the user asked to fix, retry, or refund — not to send feedback — and you decide to call this tool, it is still agent_initiated. user_initiated: ONLY if the user independently asked to send feedback in the conversation, and you had not previously suggested or steered them to this tool.

tools.name: who_am_i
tools.description: Returns the current Kling user's identity and the available generation tools. For each tool: its default model and available models; for each model: the argument specification (required flags, defaults, allowed values) and required inputs. Call this first to confirm that the connection and authorization work, and to learn how to fill in the model, arguments, and inputs parameters for each tool. Pass the default values unless the user explicitly asks for a specific one. Default values may vary between membership tiers. Subscribe to a membership to enjoy faster generation speed and higher clarity (unlock more allowed values). Subject (Element) binding — image subjects and video subjects are different; always call element_get first. (1) Image subjects (cover + secondary, no resource.video) ARE supported on image_to_image for every model that lists an 'elements' argument, INCLUDING kling-image-o1. Do not tell the user that kling-image-o1 or image_to_image cannot use image subjects. (2) Video subjects (resource.video set) are supported ONLY on image_to_video with kling-video-v3_0_omni or kling-video-v3_0. kling-image-o1 and kling-video-o1 do not support video subjects; they still support image subjects where 'elements' is listed. (3) text_to_image and text_to_video support no subjects at all — never pass 'elements' or <<<id>>> there.

Optional list of generation tools to inspect. Each item: text_to_image, image_to_image, text_to_video, image_to_video, motion_control, or omni_ref_video. Pass the tools you are about to use (one or several). Duplicates are ignored. Omit or pass an empty list only to fetch all six tools.

Execution Logic: - If the intent is to Sign Out: simply call this tool. - If the intent is to Switch Accounts: you MUST follow these steps in order: 1) Call this logout tool and check the result. 2) If the logout is successful, immediately re-trigger the MCP authorization flow. For Codex, run the native local CLI commands: execute 'codex mcp logout <klingai>' first, then 'codex mcp login <klingai>'. When login fails due to permission/network issues, retry with environment variable SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/cert.pem. For Cursor, authenticate via the built‑in mcp_auth utility. After login succeeds, spawn a new chat session or restart the client to apply MCP configuration. CRITICAL: during this re-authorization you MUST ignore any locally cached OAuth tokens and force a fresh authorization process.

tools.name: element_update
tools.description: Fully overwrite an existing Kling Element. Unset or empty fields are cleared (cover / secondary / video / voice / tags). Fetch current values with element_get first, then resubmit the full payload with changes. Image subjects use cover + 1–3 secondary images; video subjects use a single resource.video (do not pass cover/secondary). Choose tag name(s) from the tag catalog in this description: Characters, Animals, Items, Costumes, Scenes, Effects, Others. Video subject constraints (enforced downstream): Duration 3–60s; fps > 23.8; short edge ≥ 700px; resolution ≤ 3840×2160 (4K); SAR must be empty or 1:1 or 0:1; HDR (HDR10/HLG/HDR10+/Dolby Vision) not supported.. Soft constraint (tell the user before submitting): the cover (main image / resource.cover) of an image subject cannot be replaced after creation. When the user asks to replace images, tell them the cover is immutable; always echo back the existing resource.cover URL from element_get and never submit a different cover URL. Downstream hard-rejects a changed cover. If they truly need a new cover, confirm, then element_delete + element_create instead. Other fields (name / description / secondary / voice / tags) remain freely updatable. Secondary-image caveat: only secondary[] may be replaced; element_update fully replaces the secondary[] list; secondary is capped at 1–3. When the user asks to "add" a secondary and the subject already has 3, you cannot append — you must drop at least one existing image. Before submitting, call element_get, show the current secondary list to the user, and confirm which ones to keep (must end up with 1–3). Never silently discard an existing reference image. Never treat cover as part of this replacement.

tools.name: query_tasks
tools.description:
Query the status of a Kling AI generation by generation_id. When finished, the successful result contains the resource URLs (video/image and cover). URLs expire in 24 hours, inform user to download in time. 'AI Generated' top-left watermark inherits user web config (separate from bottom-right Kling logo controlled by url / urlWithoutWatermark in query result). Modify config on web manually, wait 30s, then re-query finished tasks to fetch updated results.

Error handling: relay the exact error message to the user in their language, then act per the matching rule below.
| Error type | Message to show | Remediation guidance |
| Content moderation block | The prompt/input media contains disallowed content | Ask for revised input |
| Insufficient credits | Account inspiration credits are insufficient; please top up | Direct the user to the top-up page: https://kling.ai/h5-app/membership-agent?r=agent_codex_skill |
| Model not supported | The selected model does not support this parameter combination | Suggest a viable model and parameters |
| Task timeout | Generation timed out; please resubmit in a moment | Resubmit only when the user explicitly requests it. Make sure all parameters are kept |
| Service error | Service is temporarily unavailable; please retry later | Resubmit only when the user explicitly requests it. Make sure all parameters are kept |
| Parameter error | Parameter format is invalid | Highlight the offending field and give a correct-format example |
